ceviri.20: Does the Instagram ad management service include content production, or is only the advertising managed?
ceviri.21: The service isn't limited to managing the ad budget; producing post, story and reels content is part of the scope too. Ad copy and the language of organic posts draw on the same brand voice, so the account moves in a single register.
ceviri.22: Are the account's advertising and its organic post content managed by the same team?
ceviri.23: Yes — content production and ad management sit with the same team. That arrangement makes it easier to rework creative for advertising, and it lets the formats that stand out in organic posts be carried straight into the ads.
ceviri.24: Which audience is the Instagram ad shown to, and how?
ceviri.25: The audience is built up in layers: demographic data, interests, custom audiences made of website visitors, and the broader lookalike audiences built from them. The ad runs with different creative variations across the feed, story and reels placements, and the budget is shifted towards whichever audience performs better.
ceviri.26: What happens if an Instagram ad isn't approved or is taken down?
ceviri.27: Meta's review system can reject an ad, or stop a live one on the grounds of a policy breach. When that happens the team examines the reason given, edits the image or the copy to fit the policy rules, and submits the ad again.
ceviri.28: Who prepares the content calendar, and how often?
ceviri.29: The content calendar is prepared at regular intervals by the editorial team, with the brand message and the seasonal agenda both taken into account. It goes to the account owner for sign-off before anything is published; production and publishing begin once that is given.
ceviri.30: Who keeps the password and admin access to our Instagram account?
ceviri.31: The password and ultimate admin access stay with the brand; the team is granted the page and ad account roles defined through Meta Business Suite. That permission can be withdrawn whenever you wish, and ownership of the account is never transferred at any stage.

ceviri.49: Instagram Ad Management and Account Growth Service
ceviri.50: TasarımMania's Instagram ad management service runs both your account's organic content flow and its paid ad performance under one roof. We covered this service in broad strokes on our Meta & Google Ads hub page; here we take it up through the content calendar, account engagement and the fit between advertising and organic.
ceviri.51: Let's map the scope and price range
ceviri.62: How Are the Content Calendar and Account Engagement Managed?
ceviri.63: The content calendar is built on a plan that balances different post types: feeding the brand message, showcasing products and services, and answering community questions.
ceviri.64: The editorial team first studies the brand voice and how the target audience behaves, then distributes the post, story and reels formats across the subject headings. The publishing calendar goes to the client for sign-off before it is shared; the account owner sees every post before it goes live and can ask for a revision. On the engagement side, replying to comments, following up direct messages and moderating the community are carried by the same team, so the brand voice stays consistent between organic posts and ad copy. Image production, copywriting and calendar coordination don't run off in separate directions — they flow through one team that owns the work.
ceviri.66: The Ad Targeting, Approval and Optimization Process
ceviri.67: On the advertising side, targeting is built up in layers: the existing follower base, custom audiences made of website visitors, and the broader lookalike audiences built from them.
ceviri.68: Every ad set is tested with separate creative variations across the feed, story and reels placements; the performance data shows which image-and-copy combination brings the stronger engagement. Meta's review process sometimes declines an ad, or stops a live one on the grounds of a policy breach; when that happens the team first examines the reason given, then edits the copy or the image and submits it again. Organic posts that perform strongly are backed with ad budget to widen their reach, which sets up a loop where organic and paid work feed each other. Reporting is shared at regular intervals, laid out so it's visible which audience responded to which creative. Collaboration posts have to be disclosed as advertising too;
ceviri.73: Content calendar: three post types on a four-row grid, with a key that labels the types — illustrative graphic
ceviri.74: On the left, a four-row calendar grid; each row holds three or four small post tiles, and the tiles are split into three types by a difference in fill and border. The key on the right labels those three types: brand message, product and service showcase, answers to community questions. All three appear the same number of times on the grid; no date, figure or account name is written. In the animation the rows come in from top to bottom and the key items in turn.
ceviri.84: Engagement: a post card with three comment rows beneath it and a reply marker — illustrative graphic
ceviri.85: At the top, a “replying to comments” label. Below it a post card: on the left a square standing for the image area, to its right the heading bars. Under the card, three comment rows; each row has a neutral circle (no face drawn) and a text bar. Beside the first row sit a small reply arrow and a “reply” label. At the bottom, a “following up direct messages” note. No figure, rate or account name is written.
ceviri.91: Advertising and approval: the vertical flow of the targeting, approval and publishing stages — illustrative graphic
ceviri.92: Three stages one below the other, with arrows between them. The targeting box holds three layer rows: follower base, custom audiences, lookalike audiences; all three bands are the same length and don't indicate an audience size. The approval box has a tick mark, and beside it “client sign-off” and “brand voice check”. The publishing box has a rising arrow and the note “reach is widened”. Nowhere is a figure, rate, budget or timeline written.
ceviri.104: It draws the route the page describes: the content calendar balancing post types, the engagement on the comment and message side, then the targeting → approval → publishing flow. The boxes are an example interface drawing, not taken from a real account; post and comment headings are represented by bars so as not to invent names, and the avatars are faceless neutral circles. The three types on the calendar appear the same number of times on purpose, and the targeting bands are the same length on purpose: this isn't a comparison, it's a way of saying “this type is in the plan too”. Because no measure such as follower count, engagement rate, reach, budget or duration is published on this page, none appears in the graphic either.

ceviri.135: Choosing the Ad Format and Placement
ceviri.136: The feed, story, reels and Explore placements speak to different viewing habits; the creative ratio and the message length are adapted separately for each format, and the selection is narrowed or widened according to the campaign objective.
ceviri.138: Performance is tracked by reading reach, engagement and the conversion signals coming from the ads together. The report is laid out to show which content type and which audience produced the stronger result, and it forms the basis for the next period's decisions.
ceviri.139: Brand Voice and the Sign-Off Mechanism
ceviri.140: Every post and every piece of ad copy passes a brand voice check and client sign-off before it is published. The approval flow sets up a way of working in which the account owner has the final word without carrying the production load.

_kararlar.yerleşim → placement: Meta'nın kendi İngilizce arayüz terimi. 'akış' → feed, 'hikaye' → story, 'keşfet' → Explore (Meta bunları böyle adlandırıyor).
_kararlar.özel kitle → custom audience · benzer/ge: İkisi de Meta terimi; sözlükte zaten kayıtlı.
_kararlar.Meta İşletme Paketi → Meta Business Suit: Ürünün resmî İngilizce adı; çeviri değil karşılık.
_kararlar.onay → sign-off / approval: Müşteri tarafındaki onay 'sign-off' (sözlükteki 'onaya hazır → ready for sign-off' ile tutarlı). Meta'nın reklam incelemesi ve akış şemasındaki kutu 'approval' — makam farklı, kelime de farklı.
_kararlar.69 ticari reklam kuralları: Bağlantı ticaret.gov.tr'ye gidiyor; İngilizce okur hangi ülkenin mevzuatı olduğunu bilemez, o yüzden 'Türkiye's commercial advertising rules'. Mevzuat atfını kaybetmemek için ülke adı eklendi — İYS ve KVKK kararlarıyla aynı ilke.
_kararlar.57 GÖNDERİ → POSTS: Yanındaki sayaç 12; İngilizcede sayılabilir çoğul doğru.
_kararlar.60 sizde → yours: Çip 'ONAY | sizde' okunuyor: onayın markada kaldığını söylüyor. 'APPROVAL | yours'.
_kararlar.152 kurumsal bir sorumlulukla: 'corporate responsibility' İngilizcede kurumsal sosyal sorumluluk (CSR) demek — anlam kayardı. 'to a professional standard' Türkçedeki 'ciddiye alarak, kurumsal disiplinle' anlamını taşıyor.
_kararlar.159/161/163 yarım cümleler: Türkçesi de yarım (kart özeti CSS ile kırpılıyor). Yarım bırakıldı; tamamlamak Türkçe sürümde olmayan bir cümle uydurmak olurdu.
